title: Post-Incident Automation and Review Standards
author: Asha Mehta
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the standards for post-incident review (postmortem) composition, automation of incident triage, and the operational runbooks and capacity checks that SREs must follow after any event that materially affects SLOs or user experience. It unifies SLO/error-budget triggers, capacity planning checkpoints, reliability initiative workflow, and tooling automation.

Scope: Applies to all services in the inference plane including inference-api, realtime-gateway, routing-service, kv-cache, batcher, and model-pool-manager. Does not replace service-specific runbooks; it supplements them with mandatory review and automation expectations.

1) Definitions and SLO/Error Budget Policy

- Primary SLOs (30d rolling unless otherwise noted):
  - inference-api availability: 99.95% (target) — failure = 5xx responses or timed-out requests > 1s at p50 for inference requests.
  - realtime-gateway latency: p95 < 200ms (for 1–512 token requests).
  - kv-cache hit-rate: >= 85% for customer-facing routes.

- Error budget math and thresholds:
  - Monthly error budget = (1 - SLO) * measurement window. Example: inference-api monthly budget = (1 - 0.9995)*30d = ~21.6 minutes of allowed downtime.
  - Burn states and operational triggers: 
    - Green: <10% budget used -> normal operations.
    - Yellow: 10%–50% used -> schedule focused reliability work; reduce non-essential deployments.
    - Red: >50% used -> full incident posture, stop non-critical rollouts, dedicated triage, and weekly executive updates until healthy.

- Automated breach actions (must be implemented via tooling):
  - On SLO breach (rollup or per-customer): create JIRA ticket via webhook: tags=[slo-breach, <service>], attach 30m graphs, and call PagerDuty runbook.
  - If error budget burn rate > 5x expected during a rolling 10-minute window, auto-scale capacity (see capacity controls) and trigger an on-call notification.

2) Incident Review Standards (Postmortem Template and Timelines)

- Timeline:
  1. T+0–2h: Contain and stabilize. Primary on-call documents immediate mitigation in the incident channel.
 2. T+4h: Draft incident summary in Confluence (use the template below). If service remains degraded, mark postmortem as draft and continuously update.
 3. T+72h: Postmortem draft complete and assigned for reviewer comments.
 4. T+7d: Finalized postmortem with remediation tickets and owners.

- Required postmortem sections (use this exact labeling):
  - Title (service + short description + date)
  - Severity (sev1/sev2/etc) and duration
  - Impact summary (customers affected, transactions/sec affected, estimated revenue/usage impact)
  - Timeline (chronological events with timestamps and actors)
  - Root cause analysis (RCA) including evidence (logs, traces, PromQL snapshots)
  - Contributing factors (process and technical)
  - Immediate mitigations applied and timeline to roll back mitigations if any
  - Long-term fixes and expected sprint/initiative allocation
  - Postmortem owner and fix owners (JIRA ticket IDs)
  - Verification plan and SLO check date
  - Lessons learned and knowledge sharing steps

- Postmortem quality gates (automated checks):
  - Must include at least one PromQL and one trace URL or Sentry grouping (automatically validated by sre-runbook-bot).
  - Must link to the auto-created JIRA tickets.
  - Must assign owners for short-term and long-term fixes.

3) Automated Triage and Tooling Integration

- Tools we use: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Datadog (synthetics + APM for some customer routes), Sentry (errors), PagerDuty, JIRA, Confluence, and internal bots: sre-runbook-bot, capacity-forecast-svc, and incident-archiver.

- Automation flows (examples):
  - SLO breach -> Prometheus alert -> Alertmanager routes to PagerDuty -> PagerDuty triggers webhook -> sre-runbook-bot creates Confluence draft, creates JIRA ticket with tags and attachments, and posts initial triage summary into the incident channel.
  - High burn rate auto-scaling: capacity-forecast-svc evaluates token/sec per GPU (see capacity units below) and submits an autoscale action to cluster-controller with reason="slo-burn-accelerate".

- PromQL examples to include in postmortem:
  - inference_api_errors_total: sum(rate(inference_api_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))
  - p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

- Bot checklist (automated fields inserted by sre-runbook-bot into Confluence page):
  - SLO impacted: <auto-detected>
  - Error budget consumed (%): <numeric>
  - Top 5 affected customers (if identifiable): <list>

4) Capacity Planning & Forecasting

- Capacity unit definitions:
  - RU (Request Units): an abstraction computed as tokens/sec * model-weight. Model-weight is configured per model in /infra/config/models.yaml.
  - GPU pool unit: 1 unit ~= 1200 RU on A10-like hardware under typical batching; record exact per-pool profile in capacity inventory.

- Monthly cadence and signals:
  - Weekly: run capacity-forecast-svc dry-run forecasting for next 7 days and email results to infra-capacity@redwood.com.
  - Monthly: slot planning meeting to confirm commitments for Dedicated pools and adjust reserved capacity by the 8th of the month.
  - On high-growth signals (>=25% week-over-week traffic), trigger urgent capacity review and escalate to infra leadership.

- Capacity planning checklist: (use during pre-release and after incidents)
  1. Baseline utilization: query "avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[7d])" per pool.
  2. Headroom target: maintain >= 25% headroom for regional pools; >= 40% for customer-dedicated pools during expected peak.
  3. Stress validation: run the perf-suite scenario for busiest routes (use bench-runner --preset=peak-512).
  4. Canary sizing: reserve canary pool at 3% of expected production QPS for rollouts.

- Capacity emergency steps (automated + manual):
  - Automated: capacity-forecast-svc triggers pool-scale-up: cluster-controller scale --pool <pool> --add-units <n> --reason="auto-burn-mitigation".
  - Manual: if autoscale fails, follow "Scale via cloud console" steps in infra runbook, page /eng-infra/runbooks/scale-gpu-pool. Notify infra on-call.

5) Runbook: KV-Cache Thrash (example common incident)

- Symptoms: sudden drop in kv-cache hit-rate below 60%, increased p95 latency on inference-api, increased 5xx rates.

- Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
  1. Confirm alert: run PromQL: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate{service=~".*"}[5m]) < 0.6.
  2. Identify hot keys: curl -s http://kv-cache-admin.internal/keys/hot?since=10m | jq .top
  3. If hot keys are customer-specific and high-traffic: temporarily enable per-customer rate-limiting rule: curl -X POST http://realtime-gateway.internal/config -d '{"rate_limit_override": {"customer_id":"<id>", "limit": 50}}'
  4. Increase kv-cache pool size (temporary): cluster-controller scale-kv --pool kv-pool-01 --add-replicas 2 --timeout 600s
  5. If scaling is not possible, route heavy customers to degraded-path: routing-service update --route /inference --fallback=stale-cache

- Follow-up actions (post-containment):
  1. Capture heap and op latency traces from kv-cache nodes and upload to Sentry group.
  2. Create JIRA ticket referencing postmortem and assign fix owner for hashing strategy or eviction tuning.
  3. Schedule a reliability initiative (see section 6) to reduce hot-key surface for the next quarter.

6) Reliability Initiatives and Project Governance

- Initiative types:
  - Tactical: quick fixes (<2 sprints) such as config tuning, small code fixes.
  - Strategic: cross-team work (multi-sprint) e.g., prefix caching redesign, adaptive batching engine.

- Intake and prioritization:
  - All tactical initiative proposals must include: impact estimate (SLO improvement or error budget savings), implementation owner, QA plan, rollout plan, and verification criteria.
  - Strategic initiatives require a short PRD and must be approved in the monthly Reliability Council meeting (calendar invite: reliability-council@redwood.com).

- Tracking and verification:
  - Create jira type=Reliability-Initiative. Link to postmortem when applicable.
  - Verification: after completion, the initiative owner must run a 30d SLO regression check and post results to the initiative ticket.

7) Operational Ownership and Communication

- Ownership model:
  - Service owner: product/engineering team owning feature and code-level fixes.
  - SRE owner: ensures safe mitigations, capacity actions, and runs follow-up reliability work.
  - Infra owner: for GPU pools, autoscaling, and networking.

- Communications:
  - Sev1: Exec summary emailed within 2 business hours to execs@redwood.com and product@redwood.com.
  - Weekly incident digest: SRE publishes a rollup of major incidents and initiatives every Monday.

8) Measurement and Continuous Improvement

- KPIs for SRE effectiveness:
  - Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO-breaking events (target < 2m).
  - Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) (target < 15m for sev1).
  - % of postmortems completed within 7 days (target >= 95%).
  - % of incidents with automated triage artifacts attached (target >= 90%).

- Regular exercises:
  - Quarterly game days focusing on chaotic failure modes (KV eviction storms, model-pool fragmentation).
  - Monthly runbook drills for on-call rotation members with runbook scoring recorded by sre-runbook-bot.

Appendices

A) Quick reference commands
- Check p95 latency for inference-api: curl -s "http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95,sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))%20by%20(le,route))"
- Create quick JIRA from CLI: jira create --project SRE --type Incident --summary "SLO breach: inference-api" --labels slo-breach

B) Postmortem checklist (one-line):
1. Drafted in Confluence (Y/N) 2. PromQL attached 3. Trace/Sentry attached 4. JIRA tickets created 5. Owners assigned 6. Verification date scheduled

C) Contact matrix (short)
- SRE on-call: pagerduty team: SRE-Core -> contact via PagerDuty (primary -> secondary)
- Infra on-call: infra-core@redwood.com
- Product incident lead: product-oncall@redwood.com

- Owner: Asha Mehta (SRE)
- Maintainers: SRE Tools (sre-tools@redwood.com), Infra (infra-core@redwood.com)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or after any sev1 incident.
